Incorporating the Federal Reserve’s Financial Stability Report (FSR), the tone of the February 1, 2023 FOMC statement remains modestly hawkish—“ongoing increases” in the policy rate and continued balance sheet runoff—yet is tempered by risk‑management language about policy lags, data dependence, and readiness to adjust. The FSR highlights tighter financial conditions, elevated interest rate volatility, thinner Treasury market liquidity/market depth, higher term premiums and yields, stress in credit markets (including notable pressures/outflows in high-yield and bank‑loan funds in 2022), and softening housing indicators (Zillow/CoreLogic/Case‑Shiller). These vulnerabilities increase the salience of financial stability considerations, which likely moderate the pace/aggressiveness implied by the policy path. Net: slightly hawkish but less so than a purely inflation‑focused read.
